analysis: Changed production code is limited to SSDPrefixCache.evictOldestEntry (head 1771-1780). The base code iterated a full index.oldestEntries() snapshot and retired victims via retireIndexedEntries. It returned 0 on an external change and returned the bytes freed by the first successful retirement. The head adds a !isClosed guard and delegates to SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest(index:isClosed:), which takes a closure that still calls retireIndexedEntries. That function still runs under removalLock with the hasSafeRoot/ownsEvictionRoot check (1786-1796), and ownsEvictionRoot includes the !closed and epoch checks. The change therefore tightens removal: a closed store now refuses removal earlier. Eviction is an LRU budget control (T-041 mitigation b). Refusing eviction on a closed store leaves its ciphertext on disk until a peer or a later instance handles it. The new tests (SSDClosedStoreEvictionTests.swift) assert that a closed store frees nothing and that the budget then evicts from the peer. This does not change at-rest confidentiality, because files remain AES-GCM encrypted under HMAC names. TTL sweep and the startup scan still remove expired files. SSDBlockIndexTests changes the test from oldestEntries to the new lazy oldestFirstSnapshot, which uses unsigned lexicographic ordering for tie-breaks; this is test-only. The implementations of SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest and SSDBlockIndex.oldestFirstSnapshot are not in the supplied units. Integration should verify three things in them: (1) externalChange still triggers reconciliation, and evictOldest stops or returns 0 the way the old code did; (2) the walk is bounded and skips busy or leased entries without spinning, which is an availability concern for the box-wide budget (T-016/T-041); (3) freed bytes come from indexedBytesFreed and are never inflated, so the budget loop cannot under-evict. Stage, readWindowSidecars and settleDurableDonation are unchanged (outside the changed ranges). No regression was identified against the T-041 HMAC naming, TTL, KEK purge or staging-reservation release paths.
